_comment: Per-fixture worst-page tolerances for the generated IDML/PDF corpus.
Each fixture's renderer-vs-pdftoppm output is gated on these numbers in
CI (.github/workflows/fidelity.yml -> corpus/generated/diff.sh).
Semantics: a fixture passes iff *every* page that has a matching
reference PDF page (cand-NNN.png + ref-NNN.png) satisfies
mean_de <= max_mean_de AND p99_de <= max_p99_de AND ssim >= min_ssim.
Pages without a matching reference are skipped (max_pages_with_pdf bounds
this — IDMLs that grew past their last InDesign-export are still allowed
to run; only the first N pages are gated).
Calibration: thresholds were originally sized to the worst observed page
+ ~15-25% headroom so noise does not flap. They are periodically
*tightened* (never loosened to mask a regression) so a fixture running
well below its budget actually catches future regressions.
Tightening rule of thumb:
worst_current / threshold ratio  →  action
> 75%                          →  leave alone (close to the edge)
50–75%                         →  drop to worst * 1.15 (15% headroom)
≤ 50%                          →  drop to worst * 1.20 (20% headroom)
SSIM is raised toward (worst_min - ~0.005) once there is ≥0.010 headroom.
Long-term goal stays the idea.md §13.2 budget:
mean ΔE <= 1.0, p99 ΔE <= 2.5, SSIM >= 0.99 (every page).
Tightening below those targets needs a (now generously achieved) measurement
to justify it; loosening any threshold needs a written rationale in the
commit message.

fixtures.name: layout
fixtures.rationale: Re-gated 2026-09-10 for the column wave. Two changes pull in opposite directions and both are recorded here. TIGHTER: p99 59.11 -> 54.38, because layout.fonts.sh now registers Inter — the fixture sets its body copy in Inter (samples/layout.rs BODY_FONT) and the harness default registered only Open Sans + Minion Pro, so every body run fell back to SourceSerif4 while InDesign exported it in Inter. Pages 1-4 improved on that alone (0.417/0.524/0.457/0.902 -> 0.154/0.218/0.251/0.582). LOOSER: mean 1.083 -> 1.302 and ssim 0.9502 -> 0.939, NOT to mask a regression but because the fixture gained four pages (7-10, the column cases) carrying 44 lines of body copy each — denser than anything it held before, so the worst page moved from page 4 (0.902) to page 10 (1.132). Worst across all 10 pages: mean 1.132 / p99 47.289 / ssim 0.944; sized at worst * 1.15 and worst_ssim - 0.005. Page 11 (2col-autosize-height) joined the gate 2026-09-11 and moved NO threshold: it measures mean 0.363 / p99 15.627 / ssim 0.987, well inside the values above, so only max_pages_with_pdf changed. It is gated because the rule it pins is a MEASURED one — InDesign grows a two-column auto-height frame to ten lines and splits 10/10, where we grew it to twenty in one full-width column.

fixtures.name: keeps
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with ADR 028 (paragraph keep options). Eight two-column pages on an exact ten-lines-per-column grid, each keep rule beside a no-keep control; the reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and the column split of every page matches it (also pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/keeps_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.453 / p99 9.392 / ssim 0.9698; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005 per the rule above. Body copy is Inter, registered by keeps.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED same day (ADR 026 work): the LeadingOffset first-baseline fix put every line 4 pt lower, where InDesign has it; worst page now mean 0.195 / p99 0.0 / ssim 0.9814 (was 0.453 / 9.392 / 0.9698). Sized at worst * 1.20, the p99 at the 0.3 floor other fixtures use, ssim worst - 0.005.

fixtures.name: reflow

Page 3 is GENERATED on both sides (margin-box frame, default frame options). Worst page measured: mean 0.885 / p99 24.736 / ssim 0.948 (page 3: 0.835 / 24.736 / 0.948); sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. Pages 1-2 scored mean 7.9 before the LeadingOffset first-baseline fix in the same change.

fixtures.name: swatches
fixtures.rationale: New 2026-09-08. Spot ink at full strength, the same ink at 50% through the object's FillTint, and a frame whose paint comes from its applied ObjectStyle with no inline FillColor. Was measuring worst mean 31.8 / SSIM 0.70 because the generator wrote four things InDesign does not: a spot whose CMYK alternate differs from its Lab primary (all 15 corpus spots are LAB/LAB and identical), TintValue on a <Color> (0 of 7,545), a <Swatch Color=...> alias (<Swatch> is Swatch/None 271 of 271 times), and BasedOn on an ObjectStyle (0 of 1,101 — InDesign flattens the inheritance at export). Now worst page mean 0.142 / p99 0.212 / SSIM 0.9997.

fixtures.name: tables
fixtures.rationale: Re-baselined 2026-09-07 after four table fixes: paged-gen writes MinimumHeight/AutoGrow so InDesign lays out the declared row heights; a cell edge with no declared stroke draws InDesign's default 1pt black; and a table's content is inset half its outer border, as InDesign keeps that border inside the frame. Reference re-exported from the changed IDML; all 13 pages gated (was 7). Worst page mean 0.219 / p99 2.457 / SSIM 0.9878 - tightened from 1.1/13.0/0.96, which had made this the loosest fixture in the corpus.

fixtures.name: tables-overset
fixtures.rationale: New 2026-09-07. Six pages isolating what InDesign draws when a table does not fit its frame - all rows fit, two of four fit, none fit, the header alone is taller than the frame, the header fits but no body row does - plus a 4pt-border page so the outer-border inset is measured at two weights rather than one. InDesign's export has ZERO ink on the three overset pages where the renderer drew one row. Worst page mean 0.100 / p99 0.000 / SSIM 0.9966 (p6).

fixtures.name: text
fixtures.rationale: Reference RE-EXPORTED 2026-09-06 on a host that has Open Sans, the face the IDML declares. The file it replaces embedded MinionPro-Regular — InDesign had substituted on the export host — so this fixture spent its life comparing our sans against InDesign's serif, and the old budget (mean 0.65 / p99 8.6) was sized entirely to that mismatch. Against the honest reference the worst page measures mean 0.390 / p99 0.198 / SSIM 0.982 (p6, the densest text page); the PDF also grew 13→19 pages, so every page is gated now. Budget = measured × ~1.25 with p99 left a 1.0 noise floor.

fixtures.name: text-advanced
fixtures.rationale: Reference RE-EXPORTED 2026-09-06 with Open Sans installed; `text-advanced.fonts.sh` no longer routes the renderer through CormorantGaramond to chase InDesign's Minion substitute. The DROP CAP that dominated p1 is measured and fixed — size, ink flush and body indent all match InDesign to under a point. Worst page is still p1 at mean 0.634 / p99 21.5 / SSIM 0.970, and what remains there is a LINE BREAK: the third line keeps a word InDesign moves on. Our advances are right (the same text sets within 0.8 pt over a 414 pt line, measured against InDesign's own `story.lines`), so the difference is the composer's objective, not its measure. Budget = measured x ~1.2.

The body text then lost the two words only Adobe's proprietary patterns break ("lazy" -> "sleepy", "windowsill" -> "window ledge") — this fixture gates wrap-INSIDE geometry, and those words measured whose hyphenation dictionary is richer instead; the donut page went 2.239 -> 1.156 on that alone. Current worst page: mean 2.004 / p99 79.5 / SSIM 0.9007 across 3 page(s). Held at the earlier numbers rather than re-baselined: worst + 20% would be LOOSER than these.

fixtures.name: start-paragraph
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with ADR 028 (the break-before rule, StartParagraph). Ten cases, each one story threaded through a four-page chain (a two-column frame and a one-column frame on page 1, one frame on each of pages 2-4), every case starting on an odd page; the reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and where each case's rule paragraph lands matches it (also pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/start_paragraph_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.130 / p99 0.0 / ssim 0.9884; sized at worst * 1.20, the p99 at the 0.3 floor other fixtures use, ssim worst - 0.005. Body copy is Inter, registered by start-paragraph.fonts.sh.

fixtures.name: forced-line-break
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with the forced line break (U+2028, core ab383b1). Seven cases on one page (indent + spacing, bullets, numbers, two breaks in a row, a break that ends the paragraph, justified, a break that starts it); the reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and every line of every case lands where InDesign put it (also pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/forced_line_break_pipeline.rs). It could join only once the importer kept U+2028 in the run (plugin-publish 18d0622): while it folded the break into \n the gate rendered every break as a paragraph mark and measured mean 0.757 / p99 26.6. Worst page measured: mean 0.591 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9470; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE at the time, not the forced break: in the bullets and numbers cases the text after the list marker started at the wrong x (the engine puts a space after an undeclared BulletsTextAfter where InDesign's default is a tab, and the number's tab lands at 108 pt, the next 36 pt default stop, instead of the hanging indent's left indent at 90 pt); with those two frames masked the page measures mean 0.387. Body copy is Inter, registered by forced-line-break.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 once that residue was fixed (core: an undeclared BulletsTextAfter is a tab, and a hanging first line's left indent is a tab stop; measured by the list-markers fixture): the page now measures mean 0.506 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9519, re-sized at worst * 1.20 (p99 unchanged at 15.13) and worst_ssim - 0.005. What remains is not the list markers: the 0.25 pt frame strokes and glyph-edge antialiasing (the 0.387 above was with whole frames masked, strokes included).

fixtures.name: list-markers
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign where the text after a list marker starts. Fourteen cases on one page, two paragraphs each: BulletsTextAfter undeclared / ^t / a space; NumberingExpression ^#.^t / ^#.; no indent, left indent only, hanging indents (one narrower than the number), explicit tab stops before, beyond and under the marker, and a plain tab in a hanging paragraph with no list. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export, and the x of the text after every marker matches it within 0.5 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/list_markers_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.873 / p99 33.344 / ssim 0.9096; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. The residue is not the markers: fourteen 0.25 pt frame strokes the CPU rasteriser paints lighter than InDesign, plus glyph-edge antialiasing (before the fix the page measured mean 1.114 / p99 53.7 / ssim 0.8958). Body copy is Inter, registered by list-markers.fonts.sh.
